key_insight: SPARC uses longitudinal health measurements to predict cancer-related adverse events, supporting toxicity risk assessment rather than drug discovery.
clinical_relevance: The model identified patients most likely to benefit from G-CSF, suggesting potential to support targeted toxicity prevention.
method: Transformer-based foundation model using routinely collected health measurements.
Pre-trained and fine-tuned on 101,920,379 measurements from 224,047 patients with cancer.
Pooled multi-institution fine-tuning improved generalizability more than single-institution fine-tuning.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports state-of-the-art prediction on held-out data, a same-center prospective cohort (23,126 patients), public external datasets (26,012), and two external multi-hospital cohorts (562,620 and 206,840).
watch_item: The abstract does not establish that model-guided care improves patient outcomes; prospective clinical impact evaluation remains important.
paper_title: Longitudinal AI Models Predict Cancer Adverse Events
